data.summary: The pod startup was delayed primarily by an overly conservative readiness probe configuration. The application completed its initialisation in under one second, but Kubernetes waited for the 90-second initial delay before marking the pod as ready.

findings.statement: The readiness probe has an initialDelaySeconds of 90, which accounts for the majority of the 95.95 s readiness phase duration.
The application reported startup completion in 0.86 s, well before the readiness probe began successfully polling.
The image pull took 50.72 s for a 648 MB image, which contributed to the total startup time but was not the primary cause of the SLO breach.

ruled_out.reason: While the image pull took 50.72 s, the readiness probe delay of 95.95 s was the dominant factor in the 149.0 s total startup time.
Application initialisation was efficient, completing in only 0.86 s.

recommendations.action: Reduce initialDelaySeconds in the readiness probe configuration.
recommendations.rationale: The current 90 s delay is significantly longer than the actual application startup time of 0.86 s, causing unnecessary waiting.
A startup probe would allow the application to finish its initialisation quickly and then transition to the readiness probe, reducing the total time to Ready.
